behavior: The payer's receipt address is checked like a client email: plain text and exactly one address
acceptance: A NUL, a bidi or control character, or x@bad..example answers 422 invalid_value, never 500; ordinary addresses still save.
notes: 2026-10-19 review pass by reviewer: No blockers. payer_email.go:28-30 now checks the payer address like profile/clients.go and job/accept.go: ParseAddress exact match, at most 254 bytes, valid UTF-8, PlainText. Lowercasing before ParseAddress is safe: uppercase input matches after lowering; quoted local parts are refused by the exact match, as for client emails. Real addresses still save: plus tags, subdomains, long TLDs, IDN and UTF-8 local parts, punycode, apostrophes. The pay page shows its 422 copy (pay.spec.ts covers it). SetPayerEmail is the only writer of payer_email. R-82 and api.md match the code. Minor: ZWJ/ZWNJ and space-like characters such as U+00A0 still pass, because PlainText allows them, the same as client emails. Minor: a@localhost now passes; the old regex wanted a dot. Minor: a..b@, .a@, a.@ and a trailing-dot domain are now refused; real payers rarely use them. Minor: the test has raw U+202E and U+200B in the source; \u escapes would be easier to read. Minor: the api.md payer-email first sentence is about 50 words, and D-84 wants 25 or fewer. Minor: rows saved before this fix are sent as stored. Ran: go test -run PayerEmail -v ./internal/httpapi/tests/, all 6 passed. Same test on a scratch copy with the base payer_email.go: FAIL, with NUL 500 and U+202E, BEL, x@bad..example and U+200B saved with 200. A script compared the old and new checks on 31 inputs. Latest F257-20261019T211714Z logs all passed.

proof.1: unit: TestPayerEmailIsOneAddress: a NUL (500 before), U+202E, BEL, x@bad..example, a zero-width space, a display name and a list answer 422 invalid_value; ' Payer@Example.com ' saves as payer@example.com; the other payer email tests still pass
